identity_notes: Nattokinase has a real fibrinolytic/antithrombotic mechanism supported by human biomarker studies (elevated D-dimer, prolonged clotting times, reduced fibrinogen/factor VII/VIII), and several RCTs show modest blood-pressure reduction. However, the single most important applicability caveat is a serious bleeding/anticoagulation-interaction safety signal: nattokinase is an active fibrinolytic agent, and this record set includes a case of a patient who substituted it for prescribed warfarin after mechanical heart-valve replacement and developed a valve thrombus requiring repeat surgery, plus a fatal hemoperitoneum case report — both underscoring that nattokinase should not be treated as inert or interchangeable with prescribed anticoagulant/antiplatelet therapy. On the efficacy side, the largest and longest RCT in this set (PMID 33843667, n=265, ~3 years) found a NULL effect on its pre-specified primary subclinical-atherosclerosis endpoint, and a monotherapy arm in another RCT (19786378) showed nattokinase alone had no lipid effect until combined with red yeast rice — evidence quality and dose (commonly 2,000 FU/day, i.e., ~100 mg) vary considerably across studies, and several 'positive' trials used nattokinase only as one component of multi-ingredient combination products (Nattospes, AGM granules, Nattokinase-Monascus) that cannot be attributed to nattokinase alone.
